Introduction

South Carolina licenses In-Home Care Providers to deliver non-medical personal care services. The SC Department of Health & Environmental Control (DHEC) oversees licensing.

Table of Contents

  • Understand South Carolina’s Regulations
  • Choose the Type and Size of Agency
  • Business Structure and Licensing
  • Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan
  • Establish Operations Infrastructure
  • Hire and Train Qualified Staff
  • Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans
  • Marketing and Community Outreach
  • Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections
  • Frequently Asked Questions

1. Understand South Carolina’s Regulations

DHEC licenses in-home care providers under SC regulations. Requirements include licensing, background checks (SLED), training, and quality standards.

2. Choose the Type and Size of Agency

Services include personal care, homemaker, companion, and respite services.

3. Business Structure and Licensing

Register with the SC Secretary of State, apply for in-home care provider license through DHEC, and secure insurance.

4. Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan

South Carolina benchmarks: Private pay rates $18-$26/hour, Medicaid rates $14-$20/hour, break-even 12-18 months.

5. Establish Operations Infrastructure

Set up office, scheduling, and documentation systems.

6. Hire and Train Qualified Staff

SC requires SLED background checks and training for all caregivers.

7. Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans

Develop policies meeting DHEC requirements.

8. Marketing and Community Outreach

Build networks in Charleston, Columbia, Greenville, and surrounding areas.

9. Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections

Maintain licensing and quality programs.

10. Frequently Asked Questions

How long does licensing take? Typically 60-90 days.
